sources.title: Spacecraft Fire Detection: Smoke Properties and Transport in Low-Gravity
SMOKE: Characterization of Smoke Particulate for Spacecraft Fire Detection
The Microgravity Science Glovebox (MSG), a Resource for Gravity-Dependent Phenomena Research on the International Space Station (ISS)

key_findings: In microgravity, smoke particle growth leads to larger particles compared to normal gravity due to reduced velocities and mixing.
The change in size distribution and number density affects the response of smoke detectors.
The SAME experiment provides quantitative data on the sensitivity of detectors to reduced gravity smokes.
fields.earth_applications: The smoke detectors developed from SAME can be useful in extreme environments on Earth, such as submarines or underwater laboratories.

paper_findings.text: Smoke particulate produced in low-gravity was found to be typically 50% larger in count mean diameter than similar conditions in normal gravity.
The resultant sizes were all below 300 nm suggesting that discriminating smoke from spacecraft dust possibly could be achieved by detecting in the sub-micrometer range.
